headline.headline: MARLINS STUN PHILLIES WITH THREE-RUN NINTH, 8-7
headline.deck: Miami rallies from four-run deficit to hand Philadelphia a gut-punch loss at home
headline.body:
MIAMI — The Philadelphia Phillies needed three outs. They could not get them. The Miami Marlins pushed three runs across in the bottom of the ninth inning Monday night to stun Philadelphia 8-7 before 11,041 at loanDepot Park, completing one of the more dramatic comebacks of the summer.

The Phillies had seemed to seize control when they erupted for four runs in the top of the sixth, turning a 5-2 Miami lead into a 6-5 Philadelphia advantage. Bryce Harper supplied the big blow, clubbing a home run that briefly silenced the Marlins crowd. Philadelphia added a run in the eighth to push the margin to 7-5, and the Phillies were nine outs from a road victory. Miami chipped away, however, and when the ninth inning arrived, the Marlins bats would not be denied. Three runs off the Philadelphia bullpen sealed the stunning comeback, finishing a game that turned entirely on its final frame.

J.T. Realmuto was hit by a pitch from Phillips during the contest, a sign of how physical and contested the game had become. Miami's victory drops a bruising result on a Phillies club that had led for three full innings and entered the ninth with the upper hand. The loss will sting in Philadelphia for days.

secondary.headline: RANGERS ROLL SEATTLE BEHIND FOUR HOME RUNS IN 7-3 WIN
secondary.deck: Arozarena, Pederson, Duran, and Burger go deep as Texas hands Mariners a lopsided defeat
secondary.body:
ARLINGTON — The Texas Rangers put on a power display Monday, blasting four home runs in a 7-3 victory over the Seattle Mariners before 27,683 at Globe Life Field. Randy Arozarena hit his 13th of the season, Joc Pederson his 19th, Jonah Duran his 12th, and Jake Burger his 19th, providing more than enough firepower for starter Noah Hoppe, who earned the victory.

Texas staked its claim early, scoring in the first inning and then pushing three runs across in the second to build a 4-1 lead that Seattle never threatened. The Mariners managed just a run apiece in the second, third, and ninth innings, with George Kirby hitting Elier Díaz with a pitch among the game's notable moments. The victory improves Texas's standing in the AL West as the Rangers prepare to face the streaking Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday.

secondary.headline: ADAMS AGREES TO TERMS WITH VIKINGS IN VETERAN SAFETY MOVE
secondary.deck: Three-time Pro Bowler Jamal Adams, 30, joins Minnesota as the team shores up its secondary
secondary.body:
MINNEAPOLIS — The Minnesota Vikings added a veteran presence to their secondary Monday, agreeing to terms with safety Jamal Adams, the three-time Pro Bowler and 2017 first-round pick who turns 31 this fall. The signing gives Minnesota a proven name at a position where experience matters, as the Vikings continue to reshape their roster during a busy offseason.

Adams, who made his reputation as one of the most aggressive safeties of his generation during his years with the New York Jets and Seattle Seahawks, enters his age-30 season looking to recapture that form in a new uniform. The Vikings, who are in the thick of their offseason rebuilding effort while NFL training camps open across the league, will count on Adams to bring leadership alongside whatever production he can still deliver on the field.

secondary.headline: PIRATES WALK OFF DIAMONDBACKS IN TEN, 3-2
secondary.deck: Pittsburgh pushes across the winning run in the 10th inning to edge Arizona in a low-scoring classic
secondary.body:
PITTSBURGH — It took ten innings and three hours and four minutes, but the Pittsburgh Pirates finally found a way past the Arizona Diamondbacks Monday, winning 3-2 before 15,412 at PNC Park. The game was scoreless through five frames, with neither starter allowing a run in what shaped up as a classic pitcher's duel. Arizona broke through with two runs in the sixth, and Pittsburgh answered with one of its own, before the Pirates tied the game with a run in the eighth to force extra innings.

The winning run crossed the plate in the bottom of the tenth, completing a comeback that began when Pittsburgh refused to fold after falling behind in the sixth. Enyel De Los Santos Valdez was hit by a pitch from Matt Kelly during the contest, adding to the tension of a game that stayed close throughout. The victory gives Pittsburgh a hard-earned home win and keeps the Pirates within striking distance in a competitive National League Central race.

column.headline: PHILADELPHIA'S BULLPEN WOES HAVE BECOME A FULL-BLOWN CRISIS
column.body:
There is a point in a baseball season when a pattern stops being a coincidence and starts being a diagnosis. For the Philadelphia Phillies, that moment arrived Monday night in Miami, where their bullpen surrendered three runs in the ninth inning of a game they had every reason to win. Bryce Harper hit a home run. The offense gave the pitchers a lead. And still the bullpen found a way to lose. That is not bad luck. That is a structural problem, and July is running out of time to fix it.

The Phillies are talented enough to contend. Harper, the lineup, the rotation on its best days — none of that is the issue. The issue is the back end of the bullpen, which has now made a habit of converting winnable games into losses at the worst possible moments. The front office has a decision to make before the trade deadline, and Monday night's collapse in South Florida should be the final piece of evidence they needed. Do something. Do it now. The calendar does not care about rebuilding windows.

story.headline: METS BATTER BRAVES 14-3, POUR ON NINE RUNS IN FINAL THREE FRAMES
story.deck: Lindor, Taylor, and Semien go deep as New York breaks the game open late
story.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Mets turned a competitive ballgame into a rout Monday night at Citi Field, outscoring the Atlanta Braves 9-0 over the final three innings to post a 14-3 demolition before 29,466 fans. Francisco Lindor launched his eighth home run of the year and added a triple, while Chris Taylor and Marcus Semien also went deep as the Mets sent 11 men to the plate across the seventh and eighth innings alone, scoring four and five runs respectively.

Atlanta briefly threatened to make a game of it, with Ozzie Albies crushing his 18th home run of the season to give the Braves a 3-1 lead through four innings. But the Mets answered with a two-run sixth before the offense ignited in earnest, piling up nine unanswered runs and stranding seven Braves on base through nine. Atlanta left just seven runners on base, a sign the bullpen shut down any late threat before it started.

Elsewhere around the league Monday, the Miami Marlins survived a wild one at home, rallying for three runs in the bottom of the ninth to edge the Philadelphia Phillies 8-7. Bryce Harper had homered for his 22nd of the year and Philadelphia took a 7-5 lead into the final frame, but the Marlins — who got a solo shot from Griffin Conine, his eighth — would not be denied. The Texas Rangers also romped, getting home runs from Randy Arozarena, Joc Pederson, Duran, and Jake Burger to topple Seattle 7-3 at Globe Life Field, with starter Hoppe earning the win in just two hours and 24 minutes.

story.headline: KING JAMES LANDS IN PHILADELPHIA AS 76ERS ROLL OUT RED CARPET FOR LEBRON
story.deck: LeBron signs two-year veteran minimum deal with Philadelphia, shaking up the Eastern Conference.
story.body:
PHILADELPHIA — LeBron James is a 76er. The franchise made it official Monday, confirming a two-year deal worth $8 million total on the veteran minimum, a stunning union that sends the 40-year-old icon to Philadelphia in what could be the final chapter of the greatest career in NBA history. The 76ers celebrated the signing with a full coronation rollout across their social media channels, draping the Wells Fargo Center in imagery of James in a Philadelphia uniform before a single practice had been scheduled.

The seismic move immediately reshuffled the landscape of what was already a turbulent free-agency market. With James now committed to Philadelphia, agents and front offices across the league scrambled to reassess their plans. Shams Charania reported Monday that DeMar DeRozan, Klay Thompson and Jonathan Kuminga have emerged as the premier names to watch in the market left behind by James' departure from the Los Angeles Lakers, with multiple contenders eyeing that trio to fill the offensive void at the wing position.

The ripple effects reached beyond the hardwood. Charles Barkley's renewed push to crown LeBron the unquestioned GOAT drew immediate pushback from Brian Windhorst, who questioned the logic of elevating James further based on a veteran-minimum signing late in his career. Meanwhile, Michael Jordan — the man at the center of the GOAT debate — was photographed Monday in Ibiza embracing David Beckham at a seaside lunch, appearing entirely unbothered by the conversation happening thousands of miles away in American sports media.

story.headline: GRANATO STEPS ASIDE AS CANUCKS SHAKE UP FRONT OFFICE WHILE COLUMBUS LOCKS UP SILLINGER, GREAVES
story.deck: Vancouver reshuffles brass as Blue Jackets spend big to build around young core.
story.body:
Hockey Hall of Famer Cammi Granato is stepping back from her role as assistant general manager of the Vancouver Canucks, transitioning into an adviser position within the organization. Granato, who made history as one of the first women to hold an assistant GM title in NHL history, will remain connected to the franchise in a reduced capacity. The move signals a quiet reshuffling of Vancouver's front office at a time when the Canucks are attempting to reload around their core veterans and push back toward playoff contention.

In Columbus, the Blue Jackets made a pair of significant financial commitments Tuesday that underscored the organization's belief in its rebuilding timeline. Forward Cole Sillinger avoided an arbitration hearing by agreeing to a three-year contract worth $13.875 million, keeping the 22-year-old center locked in as a cornerstone piece. Hours later, the club inked goaltender Jet Greaves to a three-year, $15 million deal running through the 2028-29 season, handing the netminder a contract that signals Columbus views him as the franchise's answer between the pipes for years to come.

Meanwhile, John Tortorella acknowledged Monday that he was disappointed by the Golden Knights' decision not to retain him following Vegas's surprising postseason run, telling reporters he remains motivated and is hopeful a new coaching opportunity will emerge. The 67-year-old bench boss, who won the Stanley Cup with Tampa Bay in 2004, guided the Flyers before departing and has drawn consistent interest around the league as a proven playoff coach. His availability figures to generate significant buzz as several franchises eye potential coaching changes heading into next season.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026
story.deck: Three franchises swap signal-callers in blockbuster moves reshaping the AFC landscape.
story.body:
The NFL offseason erupted into full chaos this week as the Las Vegas Raiders, Cleveland Browns, and New Orleans Saints each confirmed major quarterback acquisitions, triggering a chain reaction of roster shuffling that front offices across the league are still scrambling to absorb. The Raiders landed veteran Sam Darnold on a two-year deal worth $58 million, giving new head coach Mike Vrabel his first legitimate starter since taking the Las Vegas job in March. Darnold, who posted a career-best 29 touchdown passes for Minnesota last season before the Vikings opted to move forward with J.J. McCarthy as their long-term answer, gives the Raiders credibility they have sorely lacked at the position for the better part of a decade.

The ripple effects landed hardest in Cleveland, where the Browns finally parted ways with Deshaun Watson after years of diminishing returns and dead cap pain. General manager Andrew Berry confirmed the release Monday morning, eating the final guaranteed money on a contract that became one of the most scrutinized in league history. Berry moved swiftly to fill the void, agreeing to terms with journeyman Gardner Minshew on a one-year prove-it deal while simultaneously using the seventh overall pick in last month's draft on Ole Miss prospect Jaxson Dart, whom scouts project as a mid-season starter candidate if Minshew struggles.

In New Orleans, the Saints traded up in the second round to select Louisville's Tyler Shough, pairing him with newly signed backup Jacoby Brissett in what coordinator Klint Kubiak called a deliberate, patient rebuild. The NFC South division, already fractured after Atlanta's 7-10 finish in 2025, suddenly looks wide open heading into training camp, which opens in late July. Draft analysts at ESPN and The Athletic rated the Saints' overall class among the top five in the league, crediting Berry's aggressive approach as the model other rebuilding franchises should study closely this summer.
